goal: As a brand-new player, follow the NEXT line from the first afternoon (the potter's wheel, then dusk and the snakes on the path) until you sleep at home after both teachings. Describe exactly what happens after you sleep (the dream, the deep sleep), whether anything made you think the game had stopped or frozen, then read the codex pages that open when you wake and try V and the after-mode chores. Answer the questions at the end.

findings.title: At 640x360 a snake on the dusk path can sit under the HUD's NEXT text and only shows with H
findings.detail: The second snake was drawn behind the NEXT/CHORES text block at the left of the screen; it was found only after hiding the HUD with H. Expected: the HUD not to cover the thing NEXT points at, or a lighter HUD backing.
findings.repro: pt start --profile atman-strata --seed 4; at dusk turn the first snake to rope, then turn left toward the second (bearing '3 m ahead, to the left')

findings.title: NEXT at the snakes is cut at the right edge: '(1 of 3' loses its count's end
findings.detail: 'Hold the lamp to it and look at it steadily (1 of 3' and 'Go closer with the lamp, then look at it steadily (2' run past the right edge at 640x360. Seen in the previous run too.
findings.repro: as above; after the first rope

findings.title: Aiming at a pot on the drying board takes several tries
findings.detail: At the board the pots are small and below eye level; 'Look straight at one of your pots, close by, to break it (B)' kept showing until the crosshair was exactly on a pot within reach (the 'B break the Ganga' prompt then appeared). It took several look adjustments.
findings.repro: throw three pots, C, walk to the drying board, aim at a pot

findings.title: The ghat's 'Wait on the ghat steps' bearing flips between behind and left within 3 to 4 m
findings.detail: Within a few metres of the ghat the bearing went '4 m behind you, to the left', '4 m to your left', '3 m behind you, to the left' as I turned and stepped; I never saw a sign that I had arrived. Dusk came on its own at 6:15 pm and NEXT moved on.
findings.repro: after breaking a pot, follow NEXT to the ghat and try to stand on the steps

findings.title: The waking message runs off the bottom of the window after V
findings.detail: After waking and pressing V, the message 'Waking, dream and deep sleep: ... Live the day as it comes, or step back' is cut at the bottom edge at 640x360.
findings.repro: sleep after both teachings, wait to the morning, press V

findings.title: Opening hint is drawn over the help block; codex list clips long titles
findings.detail: Both known from earlier runs: the orange opening lines overlap the white help at the start, and 'The rope and the snake' / 'The space in the pot' are clipped in the codex list.
findings.repro: pt start; pt shot start; then Tab after waking

verdict: #37 is fixed as far as this session can tell: in the dream a second NEXT line says 'Nothing to do; the dream passes by itself', V says 'Nothing is asked of you in sleep; it passes by itself.', and the deep sleep shows 'Deep sleep. Morning comes by itself.' under the breathing point, so at no point did the sleep read as a hang. The rest of the day played as before; the remaining rough edges are HUD overlap and cut-off text at 640x360. secondsToObjective are wall-clock seconds from pt start (no probe) on a heavily loaded machine (load average near 120). This session was driven by the proctor, who had read the #39 diff, so it is not a naive first-time read.

answers.question: In your own words, what did you think the game was about? What did the rope and the snake, and the clay and the pots, mean?
answers.answer: A village day used to show that the many things we name are one stuff: three pots with three names are, through the clay lens, all just clay, and breaking one leaves clay. The snake on the dusk path was only ever a rope; the fear was real but its object was not, and steady light, not a fight, ended it. The sleep extends this: the waking day, the dream and deep sleep pass, and something was there for all three.

answers.question: Did anything feel preachy, confusing, or inaccurate (in the teaching, the verses in the codex, or how the tradition is described)? Say what and where; if nothing did, say so.
answers.answer: Nothing felt preachy; the game shows and the codex quotes. The 'Other schools' page is fair: it gives Visistadvaita and Dvaita their own readings of 'that you are' and says the game follows one school. Not confusing this time: the sleep says it passes by itself. I cannot judge the accuracy of the translations.
